summary: Re-review of the attempt-2 rework for task 21.9. The single open MEDIUM finding from attempt 1 (R-21.9-1) is resolved: I verified independently that the F-21.9-6 caveat in docs/testing/jellyfin-12-musl-test-host.md:396-410 and the F-21.9-6 detail/evidence/recommended_action/correction fields in docs/implementation/21.9/live-verification.json now attribute the post-fixture-edit observation to the ADR-022 durable reconciliation cursor rather than to the provider inventory cache, and that the new mechanism is accurate rather than a fresh overclaim. Specifically I confirmed against the source that a scheduled/post-scan run really can miss an item that a post-save run covers: src/ArrTags/Reconciliation/LibraryReconciliationService.cs:151 sets usesCursor only for Scheduled or PostScan; the run resumes from the persisted anchor (ReadCursor at 163, ResumeAsync at 368-388), and the enumeration loop breaks out as soon as a page returns fewer than batchSize items (lines 312-317), so a run whose anchor sits mid-order covers only the suffix of the candidate order and the rest is left to the next run. That is exactly the 'coverage guarantee is across successive runs, not a single run' semantics ADR-022 clause 7 states, and it makes the documented procedure instruction correct. I also confirmed the exclusion of the cache mechanism is correct and is now stated explicitly: LibraryReconciliationService.cs:139 calls InvalidateInventory() unconditionally at the top of every ReconcileAsync run for all sources, and tests/ArrTags.Tests/ReconciliationTriggerTests.cs:254 (ReconciliationInvalidatesTheInventoryForEverySource) loops PostScan, Scheduled and PostSave asserting each discards the retained observation sets, which is the ADR-018 clause 3 contract. The false claim is gone: grep for 'inventory cache still serves', 'Invalidate the provider inventory cache' and 'because the provider inventory' returns 0 matches in both files, and the only surviving 'inventory cache' mentions are the corrected negative statement at jellyfin-12-musl-test-host.md:406, an unrelated 21.4-section description at line 294, the corrected 14.3 evidence sentence and the R-21.9-1 correction field. The practical instruction (issue one configuration save after a fixture edit) is retained verbatim in both surfaces. Non-regression verified: the package block (619,636 bytes, sha256 3e59cb06..., md5 f3b50a91..., 7 entries, identity_matches true) still matches the on-disk artifact, which I re-hashed independently; the eight matrix rows L1-L8 are all PASS with overall_verdict VERIFIED; F-21.9-1 through F-21.9-5 keep their severities and texts; docs/implementation/21.4/ is untouched (last commit 7ad12dc); and the working-tree delta is exactly PLANS.md, docs/plan/state.json, docs/testing/jellyfin-12-musl-test-host.md plus the untracked docs/implementation/21.9/, with src/, tests/ and manifest.json unmodified, so no code, test, artifact or release-state change was introduced by the rework. The worker report at docs/implementation/21.9/worker-report.attempt-2.json carries attempt 2 and a rework entry for R-21.9-1 with the exact corrected wording and closure evidence, and the attempt-1 report is preserved unmodified. One workflow item remains open for whoever folds this review in, as it did after attempt 1: docs/plan/state.json must list the reviewer reports, so scripts/check-docs.sh still FAILs on exactly one line until it does. I recorded that as a noted finding rather than a blocker because the report could not exist before the review and the state.json reports array is worker-owned under the docs/plan/README.md single-writer rule.

findings.summary: The F-21.9-6 procedure note no longer attributes the stale post-fixture-edit observation to the provider inventory cache; the false mechanism is gone and the replacement mechanism (the ADR-022 cursor) is accurate against the source.
findings.detail: Attempt 1 recorded that the note asserted 'Otherwise the inventory cache still serves the pre-edit observation', which LibraryReconciliationService.ReconcileAsync contradicts by calling InvalidateInventory() unconditionally at line 139 for every source. The corrected bullet at docs/testing/jellyfin-12-musl-test-host.md:396-410 now reads 'The reason is the ADR-022 durable reconciliation cursor, not cache staleness: a scheduled (or post-scan) run resumes from the persisted cursor anchor and covers the library round-robin across successive runs, so a single scheduled run is not guaranteed to re-cover an edited item, while the post-save trigger is deliberately excluded from the cursor and always enumerates from the start (ADR-022 clause 6). Every reconciliation, including a scheduled one, already invalidates the provider inventory at the top of its run (ADR-018 clause 3), so the pre-edit observation was not served from the inventory cache.' I verified each clause of that sentence against the code rather than accepting it. (1) Cursor scoping: LibraryReconciliationService.cs:151 is 'var usesCursor = source is LibraryReconciliationSource.Scheduled or LibraryReconciliationSource.PostScan;', matching ADR-022 clause 6, so a PostSave run takes the scope == null path and starts at index 0 while Scheduled/PostScan read the cursor at line 163 and resume via ResumeAsync (368-388). (2) That a single run can miss an item: after resuming, the loop takes the prefetched resume page, and at lines 312-317 it breaks out with wrapped = true as soon as page.Count < batchSize. A run anchored mid-order therefore covers only the suffix of the candidate order and leaves the earlier items to the next run, which is precisely the ADR-022 clause 7 statement that the coverage guarantee is across successive runs rather than a single run. (3) The cache exclusion: line 139 InvalidateInventory() runs before the cursor logic for all sources, and ReconciliationTriggerTests.cs:254 loops PostScan, Scheduled and PostSave asserting each discards the retained observation sets, which is the ADR-018 clause 3 contract the code comment at 130-138 states in prose. (4) The practical instruction is preserved unchanged in both the procedure doc and the live-verification report. The old wording is removed from both surfaces: 'grep -c' for 'inventory cache still serves', 'Invalidate the provider inventory cache' and 'because the provider inventory' returns 0 in both files. The F-21.9-6 'correction' field in live-verification.json records the original attribution and why it was replaced, so the audit trail of the wrong mechanism survives inside the task's own report. The worker's interpretation entry also shows it noticed that the run's 'still produced RenderPassThrough' log attribution is ambiguous and deliberately avoided asserting that the specific 15:20:23Z run never enumerated the item, which is the right level of care.

findings.detail: The mechanism the note relies on is verified real, and the general statement 'a single scheduled run is not guaranteed to re-cover an edited item' is true of the implementation. The worker recognised this and deliberately avoided claiming the run never enumerated the item, which is why I treat this as precision rather than as a repeat of R-21.9-1: nothing stated is false, the procedure instruction is correct and actionable, and a verifier following it reaches the right procedure.
